verdict: Mostly trustworthy and close to complete, but not ready to hand over unpatched. Every number in the front matter, Appendix A and section 9 recomputes exactly from _context.json and items.verified.json (500 baseline records 290/122/57/9/22 with all 13 per-category splits, 2,743 reference records, 595 clusters, 159 R-items, tiers 23/45/30 to 22/46/30, verdicts 13/81/4, refcheck 2/21, 40 effort revisions, statuses 78/16/2/2, 12 quick wins with 9 at S or M). All 98 wave-table rows and all card headers match the verified tier, status, effort and wave in _titles.json, every Priority item appears in a wave, and every link resolves. The document answers all six points of the brief: shared gaps (section 2), best of breed (section 3), differentiators (section 7), nice-to-haves (section 6, W5), the three tiers, and an audit that changes nothing. Section 2 statuses and prevalences agree with the verified items and corrected counts. The problems are concentrated in the narrative framing. Six major issues: (1) headline 6 and (2) section 7.2 say Hermes stages learned skills, although verification found its skill approval gate is off by default; (3) section 7.5 repeats the refuted claim that Manus' side-effect taxonomy drives policy and adds an exactly-once ledger the card does not support; (4) section 10.1 says 11 efforts went from L to XL, but the figure is 15; (5) section 7 tags installed-app findings [REA] where the cards and Appendix A say SRC; (6) section 8 lists ZDR as a strength without saying that Priority card F-t3-005 finds it unusable today. The minor issues are softer over-claims, provenance tags, a stale tense, undefined acronyms and ADR links missing from cards. All but one have exact patches. After those patches the document can go to the team.

issues.where: 7.5 Manus, bullet 'Declared side-effect taxonomy and an exactly-once action ledger'
